classification_contract.operative_tool_call: An instruction in execution steps explicitly telling an agent to call the Skill tool, including calls inside delegated subagent instructions.
classification_contract.operative_slash_call: An imperative to use a named skill in execution steps without explicit Skill-tool wording. Still a dependency, not router prose.
classification_contract.human_only_prerequisite: Tell a human to invoke a user-only skill, or require input/config generated by one. Never satisfy by calling that user-only skill from another skill.
classification_contract.soft_document_pointer: Read glossary/ADRs/standards if present, without actively changing the domain model. Not an edge to domain-modeling.
classification_contract.plain_router_suggestion: Human-facing labels, future suggested skills, examples and workflow narration. Not current agent dispatch.
classification_contract.owned_resource: Reference/template/script/credit file co-located in the owning skill. Must travel with its full directory.
classification_contract.dynamic_call: Runtime skill names provided by user-authored map Notes. Validate model invocation and exact provider before dispatch.
classification_contract.runtime_capability: Subagents, browser/file opener, authenticated tracker CLI, git worktrees, test runner or web reading. These are capabilities, not inferred named-agent files.
classification_contract.credit_only: Attribution to copied material. No named-skill runtime dependency.

evidence_occurrences.text: - Call the Skill tool with "codebase-design" for the architecture vocabulary (**module**, **interface**, **depth**, **seam**, **adapter**, **leverage**, **locality**) and its principles (the deletion test, "the interface is the test surface", "one adapter = hypothetical seam, two = real"). Use these terms exactly in every suggestion, and don't drift into "component," "service," "API," or "boundary."
- **Want to explore alternative interfaces for the deepened module?** Call the Skill tool with "codebase-design" and use its design-it-twice parallel sub-agent pattern.

Once the user picks a candidate, call the Skill tool with "grilling" to walk the decision tree with them: constraints, dependencies, the shape of the deepened module, what sits behind the seam, what tests survive.
